messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Gibbons <laura.gibbons@atlashealth.io>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Performance & Geo-Residency: next steps (Atlas Health)

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single place to track requirements and next steps. I’ve pasted the items we discussed and flagged a few clarifying questions so our engineering team can scope a short POC.

High-level goals
- Primary use: clinician-facing triage assistant and chart summarization (text generation + streaming partials).
- Target regions: US primary, EU for EU-resident patients, APAC later for analytics.

Performance targets discussed (please confirm):
- Latency: 99th percentile (in-region) target ~250 ms for typical non-streamed summarize/gen (<=256 tokens).
- Streaming: first-chunk <=120 ms, incremental chunks ideally <=250–300 ms; tail latency for long responses should not exceed 500 ms.
- Throughput: sustained ~200 requests/sec across the service with bursts to ~700 req/sec for short periods.
- Concurrency: expected ~60 concurrent model sessions (long-lived streaming conns) during peak clinician hours; average concurrency ~20.

Data residency and security
- EU patient data must remain in EU region for both model input and logs (PII).
- US data remains in US. APAC is a lower priority but we may later require APAC residency for analytics subsets.
- You mentioned SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 — we will include those in the SLA draft.

Clarifying questions (needed to scope POC):
1) For streaming sessions, what is the typical average token output per session and expected maximum token length? (we assumed 512 avg, 2k max for scoping)
2) Are there any heavy-batched inference patterns (e.g., large batch jobs for nightly summaries) we should anticipate?
3) Which model families do you prefer (open models or vendor models) — this affects quantization and kernel selection for throughput estimates.

Attachments I’m including: redwood_perf_matrix.csv (latency/throughput assumptions) and a draft SLA for initial review.

Next steps
- Can you confirm the clarifying items above?
- If that matches reality, we’ll provision a short trial in US + EU with telemetry and a small test harness for you to run representative traces.
- I’ll loop in Dev (SE) and Priyom (solutions) to schedule a technical deep-dive.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate logistics once you confirm.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_perf_matrix.csv, redwood_sla_draft.pdf
From: Laura Gibbons <laura.gibbons@atlashealth.io>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.io>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@atlashealth.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance & Geo-Residency: next steps (Atlas Health)

Thanks Aisha — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side so the POC matches our clinical load:

- Latency: the 250 ms 99p is fine for short summarization, but for the triage workflow we need to size for 512–1,024 token outputs at 99p ~350 ms (we understand longer sequences increase tail latency).
- Streaming: clinicians expect near-instant partials. Typical session produces 4–8 incremental chunks (avg chunk ~100–200 tokens). We typically have 8–10 simultaneous streams per clinician in busy units; global peak across our org is closer to 1,100–1,300 req/sec (noted this will be regionally distributed).
- Concurrency: adjust peak concurrent streaming connections to 120 to be conservative.

Data residency: Attached is our residency excerpt (atlas_residency_requirements.pdf). To be specific: any record that can be mapped back to an EU resident must be processed and logged only in EU-hosted infrastructure; pseudonymized telemetry can be exported for analytics to US after approval.

Security & procurement
- SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 are prerequisites for production.
- Procurement is preparing a PO; please send a redlined SLA and directions for procurement/PO processing.

Ask: Can your team run a small streaming-focused load test in both US and EU regions so we can compare 99p and first-chunk latency? If so, send a proposed test plan and 1–2 times for a technical call this week.

Thanks — I’ll await the plan and the SLA draft.

—Laura
Laura Gibbons
Director of Clinical Applications | Atlas Health

Attachment: atlas_residency_requirements.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance & Geo-Residency: next steps (Atlas Health)

Internal notes / questions for scoping the POC: please review and add.

Summary of Atlas asks we need to validate
- Streaming-first workload with stringent first-chunk and incremental chunk latency.
- EU residency for PII, US for other traffic; APAC later.
- Peak global bursts ~1.2k–1.3k rps; regional sustained ~150–300 rps.
- Concurrency: peak ~120 streaming sessions.

Technical clarifications we need from Atlas before test run:
1) Exact average/maximum token lengths for both prompt and response for the triage model (they guessed 512 avg / 2k max; we need concrete numbers).
2) Do they require in-region key management (KMS/HSM) for EU?
3) Are logs allowed to be aggregated cross-region if pseudonymized? (per their attachment it sounds no for raw logs).
4) Will they accept a fallback policy that routes to a smaller, lower-cost model in the same region if we detect capacity pressure?

Plan for a quick POC (what SE will run)
- Provision two transient clusters (US and EU) with identical config; test harness will replay sampled production traces (we will accept their trace format).
- Tests: steady-state throughput profile, burst ramp to peak, and streaming-first latency tests measuring first-chunk and chunk spacing.
- Telemetry: 50 ms buckets for p50/p95/p99 + per-token throughput and concurrency metrics; we’ll capture request traces and a small sample of payloads under NDA.

Ops notes
- Model family guidance: quantized open models (4-bit) give better throughput but need evaluation on QA quality tests. If Atlas prefers vendor/model with better quality, we’ll run both in parallel for the POC.
- For streaming we’ll test both server-sent events and chunked HTTP to match their client.

Proposed times for technical deep-dive (30–45m):
- Fri 30 Apr, 14:00–14:45 PT
- Mon 3 May, 09:00–09:45 PT

I’ll draft a perf_probe_plan.md and attach. Priyom — can you own coordinating the traces from Atlas and confirm their tokenization assumptions?

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
